ai.description: *Trachischium sushantai* is a small snake with a glossy, dark brown to black dorsum and a bright yellow venter. It is distinguished by a divided anal plate and 13 midbody scale rows.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Trachischium sushantai* is distinguished by its unique, uniform dark-brown to blackish dorsal coloration, which lacks the distinct longitudinal stripes or spots found in other Indian *Trachischium* species.
ai.habitat: *Trachischium sushantai* inhabits the leaf litter of moist temperate broadleaf forests in the Eastern Himalayas, typically at elevations between 1,500 and 2,500 meters.
ai.behavior: *Trachischium sushantai* is primarily nocturnal and fossorial, spending much of its time burrowing through moist soil and leaf litter in search of earthworms.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Trachischium sushantai* is oviparous, laying a small clutch of 2–4 eggs. Breeding occurs during the monsoon season, typically between June and August in India.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Trachischium sushantai* is endemic to the high-altitude regions of Arunachal Pradesh in Northeast India, specifically found at elevations between 1,700 and 2,500 meters.
